title: Quarters of quarters, forever
hook: Add 1/4, then a quarter of that, then a quarter of that… Where does the total settle?

doesNotKnow: that the quarters series 1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + … approaches 1/3, and that a picture with three equal colours proves it

misconception: An endless sum of quarters heads for 1/2 (a quarter is half of a half, so the sum is half of the halves series) or for some untidy number like 3/8.
objective: The learner can explain why 1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + … = 1/3: at every level three equal pieces are coloured and the leftover shrinks to nothing, so each colour takes a third.

claims.source: company/domains/briefs/checks/math-wave-j-check.mjs label A5; the stage prints solid(n).toFixed(4). The reveal's value is recorded when the 'level-six' milestone fires.
claims.note: Arithmetic: partial sums 0.2500, 0.3125, 0.3281, 0.3320, 0.3330, 0.3333; S6 = 0.333251953125 = (1 - 4^-6)/3; check A5 re-run. artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/math.mjs.

claims.text: At every level the leftover corner splits into four equal squares, one solid, one hatched, one dotted and one left over, so the hatched and dotted pieces match the solid ones and the three patterns always cover the same area (each 0.3333 of the square at level 6).
claims.source: Construction in Demo.tsx: level k draws three squares of side S/2^k and leaves the fourth; each pattern's total is the same sum 1/4 + … + 1/4^k.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-822, 2026-10-14): new stage caption states the equal sizes, and the readout now shows hatched and dotted totals at every level; previously verified by fact-checker on 2026-10-14. Earlier note: Construction checked in the code: level k draws squares of side S/2^k at the top-left (solid), bottom-left (dotted) and bottom-right (hatched) of the previous leftover, and the leftover is the top-right square, so the three patterns have equal totals. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Read the construction in Demo.tsx: level k draws three squares of side S/2^k (solid top-left, dotted bottom-left, hatched bottom-right of the previous leftover) and the leftover is the top-right square of side S/2^k; so the three patterns have equal totals sum_{k<=n} 4^-k at every level. The readout prints 'hatched x · dotted x · left over y' with the same solid(level) value; at level 6 each is 0.3333 (own python: 0.33325).

claims.text: The leftover corner shrinks toward nothing (1/4^n of the square after n levels, 0.0002 at level 6), so each pattern ends with a third: 1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + … = 1/3.
claims.source: Three equal patterns plus the leftover fill the square: 3 × sum_n + 1/4^n = 1, so sum_n = (1 − 1/4^n)/3 → 1/3; equivalently 1/3 − sum_n = (1/3)(1/4)^n (check A5), the geometric series a/(1 − r) with a = r = 1/4. Builder node re-run 2026-10-14: 1/4^6 = 0.000244140625, shown as 0.0002.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-822, 2026-10-14): reveal now quotes the level-6 leftover (0.0002), shown on the stage; previously verified by fact-checker on 2026-10-14. Earlier note: Derivation: 3 S_n + 4^-n = 1, so S_n = (1 - 4^-n)/3 -> 1/3; the geometric series a/(1 - r) with a = r = 1/4. Recall (1/3 + 1/9 + ... = 1/2, by the same three-part picture) checks out. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. 3 S_n + 4^-n = 1, so S_n = (1 - 4^-n)/3 -> 1/3. 1/4^6 = 0.000244, shown with toFixed(4) as 0.0002, and the reveal now quotes d4(1/4^6) = 0.0002, the value on screen at level 6 (the stage returns to level 6 at the reveal).

recall.question: 1/3 + 1/9 + 1/27 + … forever. What does the total get closer and closer to?
recall.why: Split a shape into three equal parts: colour one, mark one, and repeat in the third. The two patterns stay equal and the leftover vanishes, so each pattern, the thirds series, ends at 1/2.
